thread.title: Northern Virginia could get a big bite of Apple

author: Daniel J. Sernovitz
title: Northern Virginia could get a big bite of Apple
text: – Staff Reporter, Washington Business Journal May 17, 2018, 1:30pm EDT Even if it doesn’t come up with Amazon.com Inc.’s second headquarters, Greater Washington could still land one of the most sought-after economic development prospects in North America right now: Apple Inc. The Cupertino, California-based tech giant plans to make a decision relatively quickly on where it will put its latest corporate campus , and Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL) executives are considering several sites in Northern Virginia that could meet the company’s needs for around 4 million square feet, according to sources familiar with the search. Virginia economic development officials pitched several locations to the company, as was first reported by The Washington Post , including some of the same sites offered up to Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN) for HQ2 — Crystal City, Alexandria’s Eisenhower Avenue corridor, and near the Center for Innovative Technology campus straddling Fairfax and Loudoun counties, as well as the Scotts Run development by Cityline Partners in Tysons that was not part of the commonwealth's Amazon bid . Greater Washington isn’t the only metro area in the running for Apple. The TBJ reported Tuesday that Apple has set its sights on the Research Triangle Park as a top contender. Participating jurisdictions working with Virginia economic development officials were also encouraged to consider sites for Apple that were not offered up to Amazon, potentially including the Landmark Mall site in Alexandria and properties along the Rosslyn-Ballston corridor. Apple has imposed strict nondisclosure agreements on its search that one source described as having the gravity of a blood oath. It’s unclear whether sites in D.C. or Maryland are also being considered. Several sources I’ve talked to noted Apple and Amazon are each in the market for large blocks of space for a consolidated campus in an area with a deep pool of tech workers. That said, the Northern Virginia sites could have a leg up given their development potential. What's more, a recent report by career site Ladders suggests Northern Virginia has a deeper bench of tech workers, with more than 33,500 corporate-level tech executives compared to about 10,700 in D.C. and nearly 10,000 in Montgomery County. Amazon is seeking to build out some 8 million square feet over time and hire as many as 50,000 employees for HQ2. D.C. and Montgomery County have landed on Amazon's short list, and a decision by the online retailer and cloud computing giant is expected by the end of the year. Apple CEO Tim Cook recently took a shot at Amazon’s HQ2, saying Apple’s “ not doing the beauty contest thing ,” but he’s also made at least two high-profile visits to the D.C. area and would have had time to eyeball prospective locations while he was here. His presence was notable at the Trump administration’s state dinner honoring French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife in April, and he had time to chat up Virginia Democratic Sen. Mark Warner during a March visit to Washington, though a Warner spokesperson said Apple's space search didn't come up. The tech giant is known for its campus architecture in its hometown. It wrapped up construction last year on Apple Park, its new, $5 billion headquarters in Cupertino colloquially known as the Apple Spaceship.
